blocks.html: Sonic Pi has built-in support for chord names which will return lists. Try it for yourself:

Now, we’re really getting somewhere. That looks a lot more pretty than the raw lists (and is easier to read for other people). So what other chords does Sonic Pi support? Well, a lot. Try some of these:
We can easily turn chords into arpeggios with the function play_pattern:

Ok, that’s not so fun - it played it really slowly. play_pattern will play each note in the list with a call to sleep 1 after each call to play. We can use another function play_pattern_timed to specify our own timings and speed things up:
We can even pass a list of times which it will treat as a circle of times:

blocks.source:
play 52, sustain: 0.25
sleep 0.25
play 55, sustain: 0.5
sleep 0.5
play 59, sustain: 0.25
sleep 0.25
play 62, sustain: 0.5
sleep 0.5
play 66, sustain: 0.25
sleep 0.25
play 69, sustain: 0.5
sleep 0.5
play 73, sustain: 0.25
sleep 0.25

blocks.html: Note that play_pattern and play_pattern_timed stretch the sustain: of each note to fill the time until the next one. This is different from a plain play, which uses its normal envelope and lets the note fade away. Stretching the sustain like this lets melodies and chords flow smoothly from one note into the next without you having to set envelope opts every time. If you’d prefer the notes to use their normal envelopes, set the sustain: opt to 0:
